Align multiline constructs — Array and collection initializer, in the language-generic spelling the export writes. Negative control in the same run: resharper_csharp_align_multiline_array_and_object_initializer = true rewrites that file, so the probe can show an initializer's column moving.

resharper_csharp_align_first_arg_by_paren #

Align multiline constructs — Call arguments by '('. Observable one key away from the export and not implemented, so a fixture would score INERT rather than measure anything: asked at true on a probe of wrapping calls and a wrapping : base(…), the oracle puts every argument on the ('s column plus one and the closing parenthesis on the ('s own column, one left of them (arguments at 53, closer at 52). Skala returns the same files byte-identical at both values. The implementation gap is a caller and not a model: LayoutWriter.Scope has carried CloserLevel separately from Level since milestone 3, and what is missing is VisitDelimited opening the Align scope with a CloserLevel of its own.

resharper_csharp_align_multiline_argument #

Align multiline constructs — Call arguments. resharper_csharp_align_multiline_calls_chain #

Align multiline constructs — Chained method calls. Observed and not implementable as the alignment machinery stands: the anchor is the column the chain's first . lands on, and that is a function of the layout rather than a source position. At 120 columns wrap_before_first_method_call = false keeps the first call on the head line and the rest align under its dot; at 70 the layout breaks before that dot too and the anchor becomes the receiver's own column. At 50 the oracle abandons the alignment for a long receiver, which is the one shape on which allow_far_alignment has been seen to matter. ⚠ Re-confirmed at the coverage pass: the oracle moves constructs/wrapping/chained-calls.cs and constructs/alignment/outdent.cs at true, and Skala returns both byte-identical at either value, so a glob on this key would score INERT and claim evidence that does not exist.

resharper_csharp_align_multiline_comments #

Align multiline constructs — Align multiline comments with asterisks. Observable one key away from the export and not implemented, so a fixture would score INERT rather than measure anything. true is the export's value, and at it the oracle pulls every * continuation line of a block comment onto the opening /*'s column plus one; at false it leaves the comment exactly as written, which is what Skala does at both values. A comment with no leading asterisks is untouched at either value by both engines. It rewrites the interior of a comment token, which no other key in this family does and which the formatter has no trivia rewriter for — and it is the only member of the family whose export value is the one Skala fails to honour, so it is a divergence at the export's own values (SK-DIV-0033) rather than merely an unimplemented option.

resharper_csharp_align_multiline_expression #

Align multiline constructs — Other expressions. Observable one key away from the export and not implemented, so a fixture would score INERT rather than measure anything: at true the oracle moves a binary chain, a pattern chain, a for header and a nested conditional chain, and Skala returns all four byte-identical at both values. The union is narrower than the name — measured, it is byte-identical to align_multiline_binary_expressions_chain on a binary chain, lands four columns left of align_multiline_binary_patterns on a pattern chain, and covers neither a chained call nor an argument list. An Align scope reads the column where it opens and cannot see the enclosing expression, which is what the pattern-chain case would need.

resharper_csharp_allow_far_alignment #

Align multiline constructs — Align even if the resulting indentation is too large ⚠ Measured 2026-08-29 against jb cleanupcode 2025.2.6, one key flipped at a time over the export in an appended [*.cs] section — the sweep's own method — and classified masked. ⚠ Not inert — the `OfInert` registration at PhaseOneOptions.cs ~1779 is overturned. On an invocation whose callee name pushes the argument column to about 98, with resharper_csharp_align_multiline_argument = true, resharper_csharp_wrap_after_invocation_lpar = false and wrap_arguments_style = chop_always, the oracle gives two distinct layouts: at true the arguments align to the far lpar column, at false they fall back to one continuation level. The export sets align_multiline_argument = false and wrap_after_invocation_lpar = true, so at the standard's own configuration there is no alignment column for this key to allow or refuse. Masked, not inert; Skala is flat at both values, so a glob would report INERT.

resharper_csharp_outdent_commas #

Align multiline constructs — Outdent commas. Masked under this configuration: it changes a wrapped list only while wrap_before_comma = true, and this export sets that false, so the comma is trailing and there is nothing in front of a line to outdent. Measured — with both flipped the oracle moves the leading comma from column 8 to column 6. Not implemented alongside the rest of the family: the outdent skips the first item, which the scope-shaped IndentKind.OutdentColumns cannot express because it exempts only the line the scope opened on.
